\label{lemma-gysin-factors-general}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}.
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $X$ be integral and $n = \dim_\delta(X)$.
Let $i : D \to X$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
Let $\mathcal{N}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
and let $t$ be a nonzero meromorphic section of $\mathcal{N}$.
Then $i^*\text{div}_\mathcal{N}(t) = c_1(\mathcal{N}|_D) \cap [D]_{n - 1}$
in $\CH_{n - 2}(D)$.
statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly. This operator also descends to Chow groups.

For a pair $(\mathcal M,u)$ with $\mathcal M$ invertible on $T$, $u\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal M)$, and $j:E=Z(u)\hookrightarrow T$, define the Gysin map $j^*:Z_{q+1}(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_q(E)$ on integral closed $W\subset T$ by $j^*[W]=[E\cap W]_q$ if $W\not\subset E$, and $j^*[W]=(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. When $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor, write $E\cdot\alpha=j_*j^*\alpha$ for the resulting intersection class.

\label{lemma-gysin-back}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}. Let $X$ be locally
of finite type over $S$. Let $(\mathcal{L}, s, i : D \to X)$ be as in
Definition \ref{definition-gysin-homomorphism}. Then
$i^*i_* : \CH_k(D) \to \CH_{k - 1}(D)$ sends $\alpha$ to
$c_1(\mathcal{L}|_D) \cap \alpha$.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pushforward of an integral $[W]\in Z_q(T')$ is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if $\dim_\delta h(W)=q$, and $0$ if that dimension is smaller. This extends linearly and induces a map on Chow groups.

$i^*i_* : \mathrm{CH}_k(D) \to \mathrm{CH}_{k - 1}(D)$ sends $\alpha$ to
$c_1(\mathcal{L}|_D) \cap \alpha$.

\label{lemma-gysin-commutes-gysin}
Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Situation \ref{situation-setup}. Let $X$ be locally
of finite type over $S$. Let $(\mathcal{L}, s, i : D \to X)$ and
$(\mathcal{L}', s', i' : D' \to X)$ be two triples as in
Definition \ref{definition-gysin-homomorphism}. Then the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\CH_k(X) \ar[r]_{i^*} \ar[d]_{(i')^*} & \CH_{k - 1}(D) \ar[d]^{j^*} \\
\CH_{k - 1}(D') \ar[r]^{(j')^*} & \CH_{k - 2}(D \cap D')
}
$$
commutes where each of the maps is a Gysin map.
